views.name: paper_author_membership
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paper.paperId AS paperId,
  author.authorId AS authorId,
  author.authorName AS authorName,
  paper.title AS title,
  paper.year AS year,
  paper.venueId AS venueId,
  paper.journalId AS journalId
FROM paper
JOIN writes ON writes.paperId = paper.paperId
JOIN author ON author.authorId = writes.authorId

params.description: Provides the list of authors for each paper with basic paper metadata (title, year, venue, journal).
params.when_to_use: Get all author-paper pairs (who wrote which paper) along with paper metadata. | Compose queries that count authors per paper or papers per author (must aggregate appropriately). | Filter papers by author attributes or filter authors by paper attributes. | Serve as a base when joining additional one-row-per-paper or one-row-per-author dimensions.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from table paper.paperId | authorId: identifier of the author — derived from table author.authorId (via writes.authorId) | authorName: human-readable name of the author — derived from author.authorName | title: paper title — derived from paper.title | year: publication year of the paper — derived from paper.year | venueId: identifier of the venue (conference/workshop/etc.) for the paper — derived from paper.venueId | journalId: identifier of the journal for the paper (if any) — derived from paper.journalId
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | author.authorId | author.authorName | paper.title | paper.year | paper.venueId | paper.journalId | writes.paperId | writes.authorId
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) over the view's grain (paper.paperId, author.authorId) — each row represents one paper-author membership | authors_per_paper(paperId) = COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId — must be computed by aggregating this view, not assumed from the view's rows | papers_per_author(authorId) = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY authorId — must be computed by aggregating this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-paper dimension (e.g., a paper_details view keyed by paperId) on paperId — safe because paperId in this view can repeat (one row per author) but the joined dimension is one-row-per-paper and will not multiply measures beyond the intended author multiplicity. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-author dimension (e.g., author_profile keyed by authorId) on authorId — safe because authorId in this view can repeat (one row per paper) but the joined dimension is one-row-per-author and will not multiply measures beyond the intended paper multiplicity. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join this view directly to another one-to-many table/view (for example, a paper_references table with multiple references per paper) without first aggregating one side — joining another one-to-many on paperId will multiply rows and thus duplicate counts/measures. Instead, aggregate the many-side (e.g., reference_count per paper) before joining. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join this view to a writes-like relationship again without de-duplicating, because writes is already used to establish the grain. Re-joining a relationship that is many-to-many on the same keys will multiply rows. | aggregation guidance: when deriving metrics like number of distinct authors per paper, use DISTINCT on authorId or aggregate this view grouped by paperId (e.g., SELECT paperId, COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) FROM paper_author_membership GROUP BY paperId). | explanation of safety: the view's declared grain is (paper.paperId, author.authorId). Any join to a dimension that is strictly one-row-per-paper (keyed by paperId) or one-row-per-author (keyed by authorId) preserves the intended multiplicity because those dimensions do not introduce additional child rows. Any join to a table that can have multiple rows per paperId or authorId will increase multiplicity and requires pre-aggregation or distinctness to keep measures correct.

views.name: paper_author_names_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.title,
  p.year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS author_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS author_names_concat
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId, p.title, p.year

params.description: One-row-per-paper aggregates: paper id, title, year, distinct author count, and a deduplicated concatenated list of author names.
params.when_to_use: Find papers (paperId) and their title/year together with the number of distinct authors and a deduplicated concatenated list of the authors (e.g., reporting, display, export). | Filter or identify papers that include specific author combinations (e.g., find papers co-authored by Author A and Author B) by using the view's author_names_concat or author_count at the paper grain. | Join to other one-row-per-paper datasets (or aggregated-per-paper results) on paperId without re-aggregation so the paper-level author_count and author_names_concat remain correct.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — paper identifier (grouped key) | title: paper.title — paper title (from paper table, grouped) | year: paper.year — publication year (from paper table, grouped) | author_count: COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) — number of distinct authors per paper (derived from writes.authorId) | author_names_concat: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName) — deduplicated concatenated author names per paper (derived from author.authorName)
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.year | writes.authorId | author.authorId | author.authorName
params.metric: author_count = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) (distinct count of authorId per paper in writes) | author_names_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName) (SQLite GROUP_CONCAT of distinct authorName values per paper; ordering of values is not guaranteed)
params.composition: This view is one-row-per-paper (keyed by paperId, title, year). It is safe to join this view to other one-row-per-paper tables or to pre-aggregated per-paper subqueries on paperId without re-aggregation. | If augmenting with a one-to-many child (citations, reviews, etc.), first aggregate that child to one row per paper (e.g., SELECT paperId, COUNT(*) FROM citations GROUP BY paperId) and then join to this view — or join and then re-aggregate at paperId so author_count is not multiplied. | Do not join this view directly to writes or author detail tables at detail grain unless you re-aggregate after the join (the view already aggregated writes/author; joining back to them will reintroduce multiplicity). | When using author_names_concat for membership tests (e.g., contains 'Peter Mertens'), be aware the concatenated string is deduplicated but not ordered; prefer joining via writes/author if you need robust membership logic in complex predicates.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need author-level rows (one row per author-paper). The view is aggregated to the paper grain (paperId, title, year) and loses per-author row detail. | Do not use when joining to another one-to-many child of paper (e.g., citations, reviews, writes detail) without first aggregating that child to one row per paper or re-aggregating after the join — joining directly to multi-row children will multiply rows and make author_count and author_names_concat incorrect because the view was pre-aggregated. | Do not use when you require a specific ordering of concatenated names or a non-distinct concatenation. GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) in SQLite produces an implementation-defined order for concatenated values, so rely only on presence/uniqueness, not on ordering. | Do not use when you require counts or name lists derived from a different join path or cohort (for example, counting only authors with an additional qualifying attribute not present in writes/author as joined here). The view joins paper -> writes -> author; any different membership logic (different write-type filtering or alternate author linkage) is not represented and will produce incorrect cohorts.
params.dialect_notes: SQL dialect: SQLite. Uses GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ...) and COUNT(DISTINCT ...). GROUP_CONCAT ordering is implementation-defined in SQLite, so the concatenated name order should not be relied upon.

views.name: author_papers_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.authorId AS authorId,
  a.authorName AS authorName,
  w.paperId AS paperId
FROM
  writes w
JOIN
  author a ON a.authorId = w.authorId

params.description: List of author-paper relationships: every (author, paper) pair where the author wrote the paper, exposing author id, author name, and paper id.
params.when_to_use: Get the set of papers for one or more authors (e.g., all paperIds for a given authorId). | Get the set of authors for one or more papers (e.g., all authorIds for a given paperId). | Join author-level or paper-level metrics to the author↔paper membership (for example to attach author attributes or paper attributes to each membership row). | Build higher-level aggregations over author-paper pairs (for example count of papers per author, count of authors per paper) by aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: authorId: the author's unique identifier; sourced from author.authorId (aliased in the view as authorId). | authorName: the author's display/name; sourced from author.authorName (aliased in the view as authorName). | paperId: the paper's unique identifier; sourced from writes.paperId (aliased in the view as paperId).
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) -- count of author-paper membership rows in any filtered selection of this view | papers_per_author(authorId) = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) GROUP BY authorId -- computed by aggregating this view by authorId | authors_per_paper(paperId) = COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) GROUP BY paperId -- computed by aggregating this view by paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to the author dimension/table on authorId — safe because this view is at one row per (authorId, paperId) and joining to author on authorId will attach one author-level row per membership without duplicating measures that are aggregated at the (authorId, paperId) grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to the paper dimension/table on paperId — safe because joining to a one-row-per-paper dimension will not multiply rows; it only adds paper attributes to each (authorId, paperId) row. | do NOT blindly join to a one-to-many table (for example a table that lists multiple keywords per paper, or multiple affiliations per author) without re-aggregating that table first or otherwise deduplicating, because such joins will multiply the (authorId, paperId) rows and thus duplicate any measures derived from row counts of this view. If you must join to a many-side table, pre-aggregate that table to one row per paperId or per authorId (depending on join key) before joining. | When composing higher-level metrics: to compute papers_per_author, aggregate this view grouping by authorId (COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) or COUNT(paperId) if writes are guaranteed unique). Do not compute papers_per_author by joining this view to another many-side table and then counting without collapsing duplicates first. | Safe composition with sibling views: this view can be used as the build block for paper_author_membership (JOIN) or paper_author_names_agg (AGG) — ensure those sibling views preserve or explicitly re-aggregate the (authorId, paperId) grain so that measures remain correct and are not inflated by implicit many-to-many joins.

views.name: paper_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  p.title AS title,
  p.year AS year,
  p.journalId AS journalId,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  COALESCE(p.numCitedBy, 0) AS numCitedBy,
  COALESCE(p.numCiting, 0) AS numCiting
FROM paper p

params.description: One row per paper with identifiers, basic metadata, and raw citation counts; useful for retrieving paper IDs, titles, year, venue/journal IDs, and filtering or aggregating by those fields (e.g., find co-authored papers and filter by citation counts).
params.when_to_use: Find distinct paperIds (and basic metadata: title, year, journalId, venueId) to answer questions about which papers meet author-based filters (e.g., papers co-authored by X and Y) when the author filtering is done by first computing the set of paperIds and then joining/Filtering paper_core on paperId. | Filter papers by year and then inspect or bucket their citation counts (numCitedBy, numCiting) at the paper grain (e.g., find papers after year N that have >K citations). | Return paper-level rows to display or further aggregate (e.g., count or average citations across a selected set of papers) provided the set of papers is determined without joining a many-side directly to paper_core. | Safe to use as the canonical one-row-per-paper source when joining to truly 1:1 reference tables keyed by journalId or venueId (many-to-1 from paper_core) to enrich with journal/venue attributes.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — unique identifier for the paper (grain key) | title: paper.title — paper title | year: paper.year — publication year | journalId: paper.journalId — identifier for the journal (may be NULL) | venueId: paper.venueId — identifier for the venue (may be NULL) | numCitedBy: COALESCE(p.numCitedBy,0) — stored incoming citation count for the paper, default 0 when NULL | numCiting: COALESCE(p.numCiting,0) — stored outgoing citation count for the paper, default 0 when NULL
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.year | paper.journalId | paper.venueId | paper.numCitedBy | paper.numCiting
params.metric: numCitedBy = COALESCE(p.numCitedBy, 0)  -- paper-level incoming citation count with NULL->0 | numCiting = COALESCE(p.numCiting, 0)   -- paper-level outgoing citation count with NULL->0
params.composition: paper_core is one-row-per-paper (paperId is the grain). Joining to dimension tables that are many-to-1 into paper (e.g., journal or venue lookup keyed by journalId/venueId) is cardinality-safe and preserves paper-level measures. | When combining with author or other many-side data, first reduce the many-side to one row per paper (e.g., SELECT paperId FROM paper_author_membership WHERE authorId = X GROUP BY paperId or SELECT DISTINCT paperId ...) and then join to paper_core to avoid duplicating paper rows and inflating citation measures. | If you must join to a many-side and then compute aggregates across papers, re-aggregate explicitly by paperId (or use DISTINCT paperId when summing paper_core.numCitedBy) to preserve correct paper-level metrics.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not join paper_core directly to many-to-many or one-to-many tables (author lists, keywords, references) without pre-aggregating on paperId, because that would multiply rows and incorrectly inflate paper-level counts (numCitedBy, numCiting). | Do not rely on paper_core to provide author or authorship-level information — it contains no author columns; use an author-paper membership view/table and aggregate to paperId first if you need to combine author filters with citation measures. | Avoid using paper_core when you need a different grain than one-row-per-paper (for example, per-author-per-paper metrics or per-reference-row analyses) because the view is strictly at paper grain.
params.dialect_notes: SQLite: SQL uses COALESCE to replace NULL citation counts with 0; no other dialect-specific constructs are present.

views.name: paper_author_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT w.paperId AS paperId,
       w.authorId AS authorId,
       a.authorName AS authorName
FROM writes w
JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: One-row-per-(paperId, authorId) link that provides each paper-author pairing plus the author's display name; answers which authors are attached to which papers and supports identifying co-authored papers via joins/filters on authorName or authorId.
params.when_to_use: Find papers co-authored by specific named authors (e.g., identify paperIds that have both Author A and Author B). | List distinct paperIds (and join to paper metadata) for papers authored by a given author or set of authors. | Compose queries that need the atomic paper-author membership (paperId, authorId) such as computing co-authorship by joining this view to itself or aggregating to paperId to count authors. | Filter or join to paper-level views after first aggregating this view to paperId (e.g., get papers with >N authors) or to author-level views after aggregating to authorId (e.g., count papers per author).
params.output_schema: paperId: paper identifier from writes.paperId (source: writes.w.paperId) | authorId: author identifier from writes.authorId (source: writes.w.authorId) | authorName: author's display name from author.authorName (source: author.a.authorName)
params.metric: authors_per_paper = COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId (derive by aggregating this view to paperId) | papers_per_author = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY authorId (derive by aggregating this view to authorId)
params.composition: Cardinality-safe to join to author on authorId (this view already joins writes -> author by authorId; author is one row per author in the SQL so joining by authorId will not multiply author-level attributes). | Not safe to join directly to paper-level tables/aggregates without aggregating this view to paperId first — since this view is one row per (paperId,authorId), joining it to one-row-per-paper tables will duplicate paper-level measures unless aggregated to paper grain. | Safe to join this view to paper_core (or any one-row-per-paper view) only after aggregating this view to paperId (e.g., COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId) if the intention is paper-level metrics. | When combining with another view that is also one-row-per-(paperId,authorId), a direct join on both keys is OK only if keys match exactly and you intend to align those rows; otherwise prefer filtering by keys or deduplicating before joining.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need attributes that are not present here (e.g., author affiliation or write-order) — this view only exposes authorId, paperId, and authorName. | Do not use when the desired grain is paper-level without aggregation: joining this view directly to paper-level aggregates without first aggregating to paperId can multiply rows because its grain is per (paperId, authorId). | Do not use to join to other one-to-many aggregation outputs keyed by paperId (e.g., an aggregated list of names per paper) without re-aggregation first — joining those can produce duplicated rows unless both sides are reduced to a common grain. | Do not rely on this view for any cohort or filtered membership that requires additional filtering logic not encoded here (e.g., time-bounded author contributions) because the view has no filtering or temporal columns — apply filters upstream or use a filtered sibling view.
params.dialect_notes: SQLite dialect (SQL uses simple JOIN syntax and column aliases compatible with SQLite).

  paper.paperId AS paperId,
  paper.title AS title,
  paper.venueId AS venueId,
  paper.journalId AS journalId,
  paper.year AS year,
  paper.numCiting AS numCiting,

FROM paper

params.description: One-row-per-paper canonical row: basic paper metadata and two paper-level citation counts (numCiting, numCitedBy). Useful to select/filter paperIds and attach title/venue/journal/year and the stored citation metrics.
params.when_to_use: Find paper IDs (one-per-paper) that meet author-based filters when you will apply author filters separately (e.g., via joins to author-membership tables) and you only need the distinct paperId list (examples validated: queries that returned paper IDs for papers co-authored by two named authors). | Retrieve basic metadata for specific paperId(s): title, venueId, journalId, year, numCiting, numCitedBy. | Start-from or filter-by a canonical per-paper row when building paper-level reports or aggregations where the downstream steps ensure paper-level cardinality is preserved (e.g., using EXISTS/IN filters or pre-aggregated author lists).
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — paper identifier (grain of the view) | title: paper.title — paper title text | venueId: paper.venueId — foreign id for venue (may be NULL) | journalId: paper.journalId — foreign id for journal (may be NULL) | year: paper.year — publication year | numCiting: paper.numCiting — stored count of how many other works this paper cites (column from paper) | numCitedBy: paper.numCitedBy — stored count of how many other works cite this paper (column from paper)
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | paper.journalId | paper.year | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy
params.metric: numCiting = paper.numCiting (stored column on paper table; not recomputed from citation edges in this view) | numCitedBy = paper.numCitedBy (stored column on paper table; not recomputed from citation edges in this view)
params.composition: Safe to join when you need paper-level attributes and the other side is one-row-per-paper (or pre-aggregated to one row per paperId): join on paperId preserves correctness of numCiting/numCitedBy. | When joining to one-to-many tables (e.g., paper_author_membership, raw citation edges): do NOT join directly if you need to preserve paper-level metrics. Instead either: | - Aggregate the detail table to one row per paperId before joining, or | - Use EXISTS/IN filters (e.g., WHERE paper.paperId IN (SELECT paperId FROM ...)) so the paper row cardinality is not multiplied, or | - Join then GROUP BY paper.paperId and re-compute/aggregate metrics (use MAX/ANY for paper-level columns if appropriate). | Do not assume numCiting/numCitedBy reflect any cohort filtering you apply through later joins — they are the stored paper columns and will not change unless you recompute them from citation-detail tables.
params.when_not_to_use: Do NOT use as-is when joining directly to one-to-many detail tables (e.g., raw citation edges, multiple author-link rows) if you expect aggregated citation metrics from the detailed rows — joining without re-aggregation will duplicate paper-level metrics because this view exposes numCiting and numCitedBy at the paper grain. | Do NOT rely on this view to compute citation counts from underlying citation/link tables. The view exposes stored columns numCiting and numCitedBy from the paper table; it does not recalculate counts and will be incorrect if you need counts derived from a different join path or a different cohort of citations. | Avoid using this view when you need a different grain (e.g., one-row-per-(paper,author) or time-windowed citation cohorts). The view's grain is paper.paperId, so analyses requiring finer or different grains must re-aggregate or use a different source.

views.name: paper_with_venue_journal
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.title,
  p.venueId,
  v.venueName,
  p.journalId,
  j.journalName,
  p.year
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN venue v ON p.venueId = v.venueId
LEFT JOIN journal j ON p.journalId = j.journalId

params.description: Provides one-row-per-paper enriched with its venue and journal names and publication year.
params.when_to_use: Look up paper metadata (title, year) along with the human-readable venue and journal names for a given paperId or set of paperIds | Compose higher-level analytics by treating each row as one paper (e.g., count papers by venue, year, or journal) | Join paper-level attributes to other one-row-per-paper derived views (e.g., core paper attributes, cohorts) without duplicating paper counts | Serve as an input for building aggregated author- or venue-level metrics after re-aggregation (e.g., papers per author, papers per journal)
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — derived from table paper.paperId | title: paper title string — derived from table paper.title | venueId: identifier of the venue associated with the paper (may be NULL) — derived from table paper.venueId | venueName: human-readable name of the venue (may be NULL) — derived from table venue.venueName via LEFT JOIN on venueId | journalId: identifier of the journal associated with the paper (may be NULL) — derived from table paper.journalId | journalName: human-readable name of the journal (may be NULL) — derived from table journal.journalName via LEFT JOIN on journalId | year: publication year of the paper (may be NULL) — derived from table paper.year
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | venue.venueName | paper.journalId | journal.journalName | paper.year
params.metric: This view is strictly projection/enrichment; it defines no numeric aggregates. Use COUNT(paperId) or other aggregates in consuming queries. Example derived metrics when aggregated by consumer: | paper_count = COUNT(paperId)  -- one row per paper in this view, so counting paperId yields number of papers in the query scope | papers_per_year = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY year | papers_per_venue = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY venueId, venueName | papers_per_journal = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY journalId, journalName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-entity dimensions on their keys — these will not duplicate paper rows/measures: |  - Join to paper_core or paper_core_5 on paperId: safe because those sibling NORM views are one-row-per-paper (same grain) so measures (e.g., counts of paperId) are not multiplied. |  - Join to author_papers_cohort (SEL) on paperId only if that view is one-row-per-paper; verify its grain before joining. If it is one-row-per-paper, it's safe. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many children without re-aggregation, because that will multiply paper rows/measures: |  - Do NOT directly join to paper_author_membership, paper_author_names_agg, or paper_author_link unless you intend multiplicative expansion (one paper → many author rows). Instead, if you need author-level metrics while preserving paper-level measures, aggregate the child first. Example safe pattern: LEFT JOIN (SELECT paperId, COUNT(*) AS author_count FROM paper_author_membership GROUP BY paperId) USING (paperId). |  - Do NOT join to any raw author-level table/view that contains multiple rows per paper without first grouping to one row per paper (e.g., count authors, concat names) because that will duplicate this view's implicit paper grain and overcount in downstream aggregations. | Null-preserving joins: the view uses LEFT JOIN to bring in venue and journal names, so venueId/journalId may be NULL. views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS num_distinct_authors
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: For each paper, how many distinct authors are credited (count of unique authorId values in the writes relation).
params.when_to_use: Return or report the number of distinct authors per paper (e.g., leaderboards, metadata panels, paper detail pages). | Filter or bucket papers by author count (e.g., papers with single author vs multi-author). | Compose with other paper-level metrics where the join must remain one-row-per-paper (e.g., combine with citation counts, venue info) without re-aggregation. | As a building block for higher-level aggregates that count papers by author-count cohorts (must aggregate num_distinct_authors after joining if joining to many-side tables).
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — derived from base table column paper.paperId | num_distinct_authors: integer count of distinct authors on the paper — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) where writes.authorId is the base column
params.metric: num_distinct_authors = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) grouped by paper.paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper-level normalization/dimension views on paperId (for example paper_core or paper_core_5) — safe because paper_coauthor_counts has exactly one row per paperId, so joining on paperId to another one-row-per-paper view does NOT duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe when paper_with_venue_journal is one-row-per-paper (this preserves the one-row-per-paper property and num_distinct_authors is not duplicated). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_author_link or paper_authorships only when those are pre-aggregated or when you plan to re-aggregate after the join — these are one-to-many (paper -> author rows) and would multiply num_distinct_authors if naively joined without re-aggregation. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many views/tables keyed by paperId such as writes, paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_authors_by_name, or paper_author_link because each of those can contain multiple rows per paper and would duplicate the paper_coauthor_counts row and thereby multiply or misrepresent measures. If you must join to such many-side data, either: (a) join to a deduplicated/aggregated subquery per paperId first (for example the original writes aggregation), or (b) re-aggregate after the join grouping by paperId to restore one row per paper. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., count of papers by author-count bucket), treat num_distinct_authors as an atomic measure and perform bucketization or COUNT(*) over the view results rather than summing num_distinct_authors across joined many-sided detail rows. | If combining with author-level views (author_identity, author_papers_cohort, author_papers_cohort_7), ensure joins are performed on authorId only after appropriately reducing the author-side to one row per paper (for example, if asking which authors belong to papers with N authors, join paper_coauthor_counts to a pre-aggregated paper-author membership that is one row per paper-author pair and then group/aggregate as needed).

views.name: paper_citation_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  p.numCitedBy AS numCitedBy,
  CASE
    WHEN p.numCitedBy IS NULL THEN 'low cited'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 100 THEN 'highly cited'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 10 THEN 'moderately cited'
    ELSE 'low cited'
  END AS citation_level
FROM paper p

params.description: Classifies papers by their citation counts and exposes per-paper citation count and categorical citation level.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve each paper's total incoming citation count and a human-readable citation-level bucket. | Filter or group papers by citation_level (e.g., find all 'highly cited' papers). | Compose with other paper-level views/dimensions when building metrics per paper (e.g., join to title, venue, or author aggregates) without changing the paper-level cardinality. | Build higher-level aggregations of papers by citation_level (e.g., counts of papers per level) by aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the primary identifier for the paper (grain of this view). | numCitedBy: paper.numCitedBy — the base numeric metric representing how many times this paper is cited (may be NULL if unknown). | citation_level: CASE expression on paper.numCitedBy — categorical bucket derived from numCitedBy with values 'highly cited' (>=100), 'moderately cited' (>=10), and 'low cited' (otherwise or NULL).
params.metric: numCitedBy = paper.numCitedBy (base attribute / numeric value, not an aggregate within this view) | citation_level = CASE WHEN paper.numCitedBy IS NULL THEN 'low cited' WHEN paper.numCitedBy >= 100 THEN 'highly cited' WHEN paper.numCitedBy >= 10 THEN 'moderately cited' ELSE 'low cited' END (deterministic bucket expression derived from numCitedBy)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any paper-level dimension or normalized paper views (e.g., paper_core, paper_core_5, paper_with_venue_journal) ON paperId — safe because those views are one-row-per-paper, so this view's per-paper measures (numCitedBy, citation_level) will not be duplicated. | Safe to join to author-facing paper aggregates that are also one-row-per-paper (e.g., paper_authors_by_name if it is normalized to one row per paper) on paperId — verify the sibling view's grain is one-row-per-paper before joining. | Do NOT directly join this view to true one-to-many child tables/views (for example: paper_author_membership, paper_author_link, paper_authorships, paper_author_names_agg, paper_coauthor_counts) on paperId without re-aggregating, because those joins will multiply rows per paper and therefore duplicate/overcount numCitedBy and any aggregates derived from it. If you must join to a one-to-many relation, either: |   - Aggregate the child relation up to paperId first (e.g., COUNT(authorId) AS num_authors per paper) and then join the aggregated result to this view on paperId, or |   - Use this view as the driving table and compute metrics that explicitly account for the multiplicity (for example, compute SUM(numCitedBy) only after deduplicating to one row per paper). | When composing into higher-level metrics (e.g., counts of highly cited papers per author), join author-paper link tables by paperId to map papers to authors, but ensure you aggregate after the join at the desired grain (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) FILTER (citation_level = 'highly cited') per author) to avoid duplicating numCitedBy values. | If combining with sibling AGG views (e.g., paper_coauthor_counts), confirm those sibling views are also one-row-per-paper; if they are aggregated at paper grain, joining on paperId is safe and will not duplicate measures.

FROM paper p

params.description: Provides one-row-per-paper membership of the paper's publishing venue (venue id, name, and paper year).
params.when_to_use: When you need to list which venue a specific paper was published in (paper-level enrichment). | When composing paper-level reports that include venue name or venue id alongside paper identifiers or year. | As a joinable paper-level dimension when aggregating metrics by venue or year (after appropriate grouping). | When filtering or slicing paper sets by venueId, venueName, or year before further aggregation.

Grain: one row per paperId. | venueId: identifier of the venue where the paper was published — derived from table paper.venueId (SELECT alias p.venueId AS venueId). Nullable values are filtered out by the view WHERE clause (venueId IS NOT NULL). | venueName: human-readable name of the venue — derived from table venue.venueName (SELECT alias v.venueName AS venueName). This is taken from the joined venue row matched by venueId. | year: publication year of the paper — derived from table paper.year (SELECT alias p.year AS year).
params.metric: This view contains no derived numeric metrics/aggregates. All outputs are identity columns mapped from base tables. | If used as the basis for metrics, common derived metrics would be computed after composition, for example: | count_papers = COUNT(paperId)  -- aggregation applied at the consumer level (grouping by venueId or year as needed).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or any other one-row-per-paper view such as paper_core_5) on paperId — safe because venue_with_paper_membership is one-row-per-paper, so joining on paperId does not duplicate paper-level rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to venue-level dimension (e.g., a view that is one-row-per-venue keyed by venueId) on venueId — safe because venue is one-row-per-venue and venue_with_paper_membership has at most one matching venue row per paper, so measures at the paper grain are preserved. | DO NOT join this view directly to one-to-many children of paper (for example paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_authors_by_name, paper_author_names_agg without re-aggregation) if you intend to preserve paper-level counts/metrics — such joins will multiply rows per paper and thus duplicate any paper-level measures unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you must combine with a paper -> many relation (e.g., paper_authorships or paper_author_membership), either: |   - aggregate the many-side first to one row per paper (e.g., author counts per paper) and then join, or |   - join and then compute metrics with DISTINCT keys or use COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) to avoid double-counting. | When grouping by venueId or venueName, it is safe to aggregate directly from this view (e.g., COUNT(paperId) grouped by venueId) because the view's grain is paperId and each paper maps to a single venue in the view. | Because the view filters WHERE p.venueId IS NOT NULL, joining to venue or grouping by venueId from this view will not include papers lacking a venue; if you need to include venue-less papers, use the base paper table or a different view.

views.name: papers_per_venue_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.venueId AS venueId,
  v.venueName AS venueName,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.paperId) AS paper_count
FROM venue v
JOIN paper p ON v.venueId = p.venueId
WHERE p.venueId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY v.venueId, v.venueName

params.description: Counts of distinct papers published at each venue (one row per venue).
params.when_to_use: Get the number of unique papers for each venue (venue-level paper counts). | Compose venue-level reports or dashboards showing publications per venue. | Join venue-level paper counts to venue metadata or filter/compare venues by publication volume. | Use as a pre-aggregated input when computing rates or ratios per venue (e.g., citations per paper) provided downstream joins do not duplicate venue rows.
params.output_schema: venueId: the unique identifier for the venue — derived from venue.venueId (base table column v.venueId). | venueName: the human-readable name of the venue — derived from venue.venueName (base table column v.venueName). | paper_count: the number of distinct papers associated with the venue — derived as COUNT(DISTINCT p.paperId) over paper.paperId (base table column p.paperId).
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paper.paperId) grouped by venue.venueId, venue.venueName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to venue (or other one-row-per-venue dimension) on venueId — safe because this view is one-row-per-venue, so joining another one-row-per-venue table/view preserves row cardinality and does NOT duplicate paper_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to aggregated venue-level metrics (e.g., another AGG that is one-row-per-venue) on venueId — safe because both sides are aggregated to the same grain (venue), avoiding duplication of measures. | do NOT join directly to paper (the base table) on venueId without re-aggregation — unsafe because paper is many-to-one to venue and joining would duplicate the paper_count measure for each paper row, inflating counts. | do NOT join to one-to-many child tables of venue (for example, paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_authors_by_name, paper_authorships JOINs or other per-paper/per-author tables) without first aggregating those tables to venueId — unsafe because those joins would multiply rows per venue and thereby multiply paper_count unless you re-aggregate (e.g., recompute COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) after the join). | If combining this view with other one-to-many datasets, either: (a) pre-aggregate the one-to-many dataset to the venueId grain before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate using COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) or equivalent to restore correct counts. | When composing into larger queries, treat paper_count as a stable venue-level metric; do not sum paper_count across joined detail rows without ensuring deduplication by venueId.

views.name: paper_with_venue
views.body_sql:
SELECT

params.description: A per-paper view that returns core paper attributes plus its venue name and citation counts (incoming and outgoing).
params.when_to_use: Get a single row per paper with metadata and citation counts (e.g., show paper details in UI). | Base for filtering or aggregating papers by venue, year, or citation counts. | Compose into higher-level metrics by joining on paperId (e.g., compute author aggregates by summing paper-level citation counts).
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — from paper_core.paperId | title: paper title (string) — from paper_core.title | year: publication year (int, may be null) — from paper_core.year | venueId: identifier of the venue where the paper was published (may be null) — from paper_core.venueId | venueName: human-readable venue name (may be null) — from venue.venueName (joined via venue.venueId = paper_core.venueId) | numCitedBy: number of distinct incoming citations reported on the paper — from paper_core.numCitedBy (treated as a pre-computed metric on paper_core) | numCiting: number of distinct outgoing citations reported on the paper — from paper_core.numCiting (treated as a pre-computed metric on paper_core)
params.grounded_columns: paper_core.paperId | paper_core.title | paper_core.year | paper_core.venueId | paper_core.numCitedBy | paper_core.numCiting | venue.venueId | venue.venueName
params.metric: numCitedBy = paper_core.numCitedBy  -- treat as a precomputed per-paper metric (COUNT/DISTINCT of inbound citations performed upstream in paper_core) | numCiting = paper_core.numCiting    -- treat as a precomputed per-paper metric (COUNT/DISTINCT of outbound citations performed upstream in paper_core)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension that is one-row-per-key without re-aggregation. Examples: |   - Safe: join to paper_core (or paper_core_5) on paperId — safe because this view is one-row-per paperId and paper_core is the normalized source of the same one-row-per-paper grain. |   - Safe: join to venue (or paper_with_venue_journal) on venueId — safe because venue is one-row-per-venueId; joining preserves one row per paper and does NOT duplicate numCitedBy/numCiting. |   - Safe: join to author_identity on authorId (when you first aggregate paper-level measures to author-level) only if you have already aggregated or will aggregate by author; do NOT directly join this view to a many-to-many authorship table without aggregation. | cardinality-UNSAFE joins (avoid or re-aggregate after join): |   - Do NOT directly join to paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_author_link, paper_authors_by_name, paper_author_names_agg, or paper_authors_* style JOIN/RESHAPE views on paperId and authorId without aggregation, because those are one-to-many (paper -> multiple authors). Joining them directly will multiply rows for a paper and thus multiply numCitedBy/numCiting incorrectly. |   - Do NOT directly join to paper_coauthor_counts or other paper-level aggregations that are one-row-per-paper-per-something without checking their grain — if they are one-to-many relative to paperId, you must first aggregate them to one row per paperId before joining. | Recommended safe patterns when combining with many-to-many detail: |   - If you need author-level aggregates (e.g., sum of citations for an author): start from a one-row-per-paper source (this view), join to paper_authorships (or paper_author_membership) to get author keys, then GROUP BY authorId and SUM(numCitedBy) / SUM(numCiting). This re-aggregates and prevents duplication. |   - If you need to attach lists of authors or other repeating details to each paper for display, perform the join but compute/display non-aggregated repeating columns (e.g., author names) only; do not SUM numCitedBy/numCiting after such a join unless you first collapse duplicates (e.g., using DISTINCT on paperId) or re-aggregate. | Summary: This view is one-row-per paperId; safe to join with other one-row-per-key dimensions (venue, normalized paper_core). Avoid direct joins to one-to-many relationship tables without re-aggregation, because those will multiply the per-paper metrics numCitedBy and numCiting.

views.name: paper_core_18
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paper.paperId AS paperId,
  paper.title AS title,
  paper.venueId AS venueId,
  paper.journalId AS journalId,
  paper.year AS year,
  paper.numCiting AS numCiting,
  paper.numCitedBy AS numCitedBy
FROM paper

params.description: One-row-per-paper core record with bibliographic identifiers and citation counts (answers questions about a paper's identity and citation metrics).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve basic metadata for a specific paperId (title, venueId, journalId, year) and its citation counts. | Compose higher-level metrics that need per-paper citation counts (e.g., average citations per paper in an author cohort) by aggregating this view. | Filter papers by year, venueId, journalId or citation thresholds as a building block for downstream joins or aggregations.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier for the paper; derived directly from paper.paperId | title: paper title text; derived directly from paper.title | venueId: identifier of the venue (conference/workshop) associated with the paper; derived directly from paper.venueId | journalId: identifier of the journal associated with the paper (if any); derived directly from paper.journalId | year: publication year of the paper; derived directly from paper.year | numCiting: number of outgoing citation relationships from this paper (i.e., how many papers this paper cites) ; derived directly from paper.numCiting | numCitedBy: number of incoming citation relationships to this paper (i.e., how many papers cite this paper); derived directly from paper.numCitedBy
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | paper.journalId | paper.year | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy
params.metric: numCiting = direct base metric stored on paper.numCiting (not an aggregate in this view) | numCitedBy = direct base metric stored on paper.numCitedBy (not an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension that is one-row-per-paper on paperId (for example, other normalized paper-core views keyed by paperId) — safe because paper_core_18 has one row per paperId so the measures numCiting and numCitedBy will not be duplicated when joined one-to-one on paperId. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-venue view/table on venueId — safe because venue-level tables are expected to be one row per venueId; the paper-level measures remain per-paper and are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-journal view/table on journalId — safe for the same reason as venues. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by paperId (for example: paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_author_names_agg, paper_authors_by_name, paper_coauthor_counts, or any author-paper join/aggregation) without re-aggregating after the join because those joins will multiply rows for a single paper and thus duplicate this view's per-paper measures (numCiting, numCitedBy). If you need author-level or per-paper-per-author results, either: | - aggregate paper_core_18 after joining to the one-to-many table back to one row per paper (e.g., sum/avg over distinct paperId as appropriate), or | - first aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per paperId (e.g., collect authors as array, count coauthors per paper) and then join to this view (safe), or | - join this view to the one-to-many table and then compute measures using DISTINCT paperId or window functions that avoid double-counting. | example safe composition patterns: | - To compute total citations for an author cohort: join author_papers_cohort (which selects paperId for the cohort) to paper_core_18 on paperId and then SUM(numCitedBy) grouped by the cohort identifier — this is safe because author_papers_cohort should present one row per paper in the cohort (if it contains duplicates, deduplicate paperId first). | - To enrich paper records with venue/journal metadata: join paper_core_18 -> venue_table on venueId and/or -> journal_table on journalId (one-to-one), which will not duplicate per-paper metrics. | note on duplicates in sibling views: some sibling views (e.g., paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_authors_by_name) are explicitly joins/reshapes that create multiple rows per paper for each author; do not join those directly without handling multiplicity as described above.

views.description: One-row-per-paper core record with bibliographic identifiers and citation counts (answers questions about a paper's identity and citation metrics).

views.name: paper_coauthor_pairs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS author_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS author_ids,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS author_names
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregation of distinct authors: number of distinct authors and comma-concatenated distinct author IDs and author names, one row per paperId.
params.when_to_use: Find which papers have particular combinations of authors (e.g., papers co-authored by X and Y) by checking membership in the comma-concatenated author_ids or by joining/splitting author_ids — validated by the question that correctly found papers co-authored by Peter Mertens and Dina Barbian. | Report the count of distinct authors per paper (author_count) for analyses that require one row per paper (e.g., compute average authors per paper by aggregating author_count over papers). | Display or export the set of author IDs and/or author names associated with each paper (as comma-separated lists).
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — paper identifier (grouping key) | author_count: COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) — number of distinct authors on the paper | author_ids: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) — comma-separated distinct authorId values (string) | author_names: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName) — comma-separated distinct authorName values (string)
params.metric: author_count = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId)  -- distinct author count per paperId (computed in the view)
params.composition: Safe to join one-to-one or many-to-one into this view on paperId from tables/views that are strictly one-row-per-paper (e.g., other paper-level tables) because this view is one row per paperId. | Do NOT join this view directly to writes (or other paper->author one-to-many tables) without re-aggregating the result back to paperId, because such a join will expand rows and invalidate author_count and duplicate concatenated lists. | If you need to attach author-level attributes, join to a deduplicated author table keyed by authorId derived separately (not by exploding the concatenated strings), then re-aggregate by paperId if you must preserve per-paper metrics.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view when you need one row per author-paper pair or any author-level attribute expanded into separate rows: the view is aggregated to one row per paperId (wrong grain) and will not provide per-author rows. | Do not join this view to writes (or other paper->author one-to-many tables) expecting to preserve author_count without re-aggregation: joining to the underlying one-to-many tables will multiply rows and distort counts because this view already condensed writes via COUNT(DISTINCT) and GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT). | Do not rely on the order or parsing of author_names/author_ids for positional matching between IDs and names: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ...) in SQLite does not guarantee a deterministic pairing or order between the two concatenated columns, so you cannot assume the Nth id corresponds to the Nth name.
params.dialect_notes: This SQL uses SQLite GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ...) semantics. GROUP_CONCAT in SQLite produces a comma-separated string and does not guarantee ordering; therefore the relative order between author_ids and author_names is not reliable.

views.description: Per-paper aggregation of distinct authors: number of distinct authors and comma-concatenated distinct author IDs and author names, one row per paperId.
validated_on: Which papers were co-authored by both Peter Mertens and Dina Barbian? Return their paper IDs.

views.name: paper_authorship
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  w.authorId AS authorId,
  a.authorName AS authorName,
  p.numCitedBy AS numCitedBy
FROM paper p
JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: Row-level join of papers to their authors, exposing each paper-author pair with the author's name and the paper's citation count.
params.when_to_use: Get the list of authors for each paper including author names and how many times the paper was cited (paper-level citation metric) — e.g., show all authors for a paper and the paper's impact. | Compose further aggregations at the author or paper grain (e.g., total citations per author, number of papers per author) by treating this view as the canonical paper-author grain. | Filter papers or authors and then compute derived metrics that aggregate numCitedBy across the paper-author pairs (with attention to duplication guidance below). | Join with paper- or author-level dimensions when building reporting tables that need both the paper-author relationship and descriptive attributes of paper or author.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper; derives from paper.paperId (base table column in the FROM). | authorId: identifier of the author who wrote the paper; derives from writes.authorId (base table column in the JOIN). | authorName: display name of the author; derives from author.authorName (base table column in the JOIN). | numCitedBy: citation count for the paper (paper-level metric); derives from paper.numCitedBy (base table column in the FROM).
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.numCitedBy | writes.paperId | writes.authorId | author.authorId | author.authorName
params.metric: numCitedBy = paper.numCitedBy (a native column on the paper table; NOT an aggregate in this view — it is a paper-level attribute carried to each paper-author row).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or any paper-level dimension view) on paperId — safe because paper_core is one-row-per-paper, so joining will not multiply paper-level measures in this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity (or any author-level dimension view) on authorId — safe because author_identity is one-row-per-author, so author attributes can be added without duplicating rows or measures. | DO NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views that expand authors per paper (for example another writes-like table or a reshaped authors list that repeats author rows) without first aggregating or deduplicating, because such joins would multiply rows and duplicate the paper.numCitedBy value across the expanded rows. | DO NOT join this view to coauthor- or contribution-aggregation views that are one-to-many with respect to (paperId, authorId) unless those views have been reduced to the same grain; otherwise numCitedBy will be counted multiple times when aggregating. | When aggregating numCitedBy to author-level metrics (e.g., total citations per author), first reduce this view by paperId to avoid double-counting when an author has multiple rows per paper (not applicable here because grain is already one-row-per (paperId, authorId)). Example safe pattern: SELECT authorId, SUM(numCitedBy) AS totalCitations FROM paper_authorship GROUP BY authorId — this sums each paper's citation count once per authored paper. | If combining with sibling view paper_coauthor_counts (AGG) or paper_author_names_agg (AGG), ensure those sibling views are at compatible grains: join only on paperId after ensuring the sibling is one-row-per-paper (or aggregate it to one-row-per-paper) to avoid duplicating numCitedBy. | If building author-level cohorts using author_papers_cohort or author_papers_cohort_7 (SEL), prefer performing author-level aggregation on paper_authorship first (group by authorId) and then joining to the cohort view on authorId — this preserves correct accounting of paper.numCitedBy.
