SELECT DISTINCT pam.paperId
FROM paper_author_membership AS pam
WHERE 1=1

params.description: List of distinct paper identifiers for papers that have any author membership record (one row per paperId).
params.when_to_use: Get the set of papers that appear in the paper_author_membership table (e.g., to limit further analysis to papers with author membership). | As a driving cohort when composing additional paper-level metrics (counts, attributes) while guaranteeing one-row-per-paper granularity. | Filter or semi-join other paper-level views/tables to only those papers known to have author membership records.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of a paper; derived directly from paper_author_membership.paperId (DISTINCT).
params.metric: paper_count_cohort = COUNT(DISTINCT paper_author_membership.paperId)  -- when aggregated, the cohort size is the distinct count of paperId in paper_author_membership
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or paper_core_5) on paperId — safe because paper_core is normalized one-row-per-paper, so joining will not duplicate rows from this view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe because paper_with_venue_journal is a paper-level (one-row-per-paper) join and will not multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_papers_cohort (SEL) on paperId — safe if author_papers_cohort is also one-row-per-paper; verify its grain before joining. | do NOT directly join to paper_author_membership (JOIN), paper_authorships (JOIN), paper_author_names_agg (AGG), paper_coauthor_counts (AGG), paper_authors_by_name (RESHAPE), paper_author_link (JOIN) or any other one-to-many author-level tables on paperId without re-aggregating first — those are one-to-many relative to paperId and will duplicate this view's single row per paper and inflate any measures derived from it. | If you need author-level detail, first aggregate the author-level table to one-row-per-paper (for example, count of authors per paper, coauthor counts, or concatenated author names) and then join the aggregated result to this view on paperId to preserve correct cardinality.

views.description: List of distinct paper identifiers for papers that have any author membership record (one row per paperId).

views.name: paper_dataset_links
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paperId,
  datasetId
FROM paperDataset

params.description: Lists every (paper, dataset) relationship recorded in the paperDataset table — i.e., which datasets are linked to which papers.
params.when_to_use: Find all datasets referenced by a given paper or set of papers. | Find all papers that reference a given dataset or set of datasets. | Use as the grain when counting distinct datasets per paper or distinct papers per dataset (after applying appropriate aggregation). | Compose with paper or dataset dimension views to enrich links with paper or dataset attributes without duplicating link rows.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived directly from base column paperDataset.paperId | datasetId: identifier of the dataset — derived directly from base column paperDataset.datasetId
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- implicit measure: counts of (paperId, datasetId) link rows at the view grain | distinct_papers = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId)  -- when aggregated over a selection of datasetIds or whole view | distinct_datasets = COUNT(DISTINCT datasetId)  -- when aggregated over a selection of paperIds or whole view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a paper-level dimension (e.g., paper_core or paper_core_5) on paperId — safe because paper_core is one-row-per-paper and this view is one-row-per-(paperId,datasetId); joining preserves one link row per dataset and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dataset dimension (if available) on datasetId — safe because a well-formed dataset dimension is one-row-per-dataset; joining preserves link granularity and does not duplicate measures. | do NOT join directly to a one-to-many table from paper (for example, a papers->authors membership table like paper_author_membership) without aggregation on the appended side first, because joining a one-row-per-(paper,dataset) link to a one-to-many paper->author relationship will multiply link rows for papers with multiple authors and thus duplicate counts/metrics derived from this view. | do NOT join to any view that is many-to-many with paperId (or datasetId) on the same key without re-aggregation; instead aggregate the many-side to one-row-per-key (e.g., authors aggregated by paperId) before joining to preserve correct counts. | safe composition pattern: to get 'datasets per paper' counts, group this view by paperId and COUNT(DISTINCT datasetId) (or COUNT(*) if uniqueness is guaranteed), then join the aggregated result to paper_core on paperId. | safe composition pattern: to get 'papers per dataset' counts, group this view by datasetId and COUNT(DISTINCT paperId), then join the aggregated result to a dataset dimension on datasetId.

views.description: Lists every (paper, dataset) relationship recorded in the paperDataset table — i.e., which datasets are linked to which papers.

views.name: paper_distinct_dataset_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pd.datasetId) AS distinct_dataset_count
FROM paper AS p
JOIN paperDataset AS pd ON p.paperId = pd.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper counts of distinct datasets referenced by that paper (one row per paper).
params.when_to_use: Get how many unique datasets each paper mentions or uses. | Filter or rank papers by the number of distinct datasets they reference. | Serve as a foundation for further aggregation (e.g., average distinct_dataset_count by venue, author, year) when composed correctly.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper (derived from paper.paperId) | distinct_dataset_count: number of unique datasets associated with the paper (COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId))
params.metric: distinct_dataset_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId) grouped by paper.paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional / one-row-per-paper views on paperId — e.g., join to paper_core (paper_core.paperId = paper_distinct_dataset_counts.paperId) — safe because paper_distinct_dataset_counts has exactly one row per paperId so its measure distinct_dataset_count will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to normalized paper views that are one-row-per-paper (paper_core_5, paper_with_venue_journal if normalized to one row per paper) on paperId — safe for the same reason. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many child tables or join-views that expand rows per paper (examples: paperDataset, paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_author_link, paper_authors_by_name, paper_authorships JOINs) without re-aggregation — joining those will multiply rows per paper and therefore inflate distinct_dataset_count unless you re-aggregate (e.g., SUM(distinct_dataset_count) after grouping by paper or recompute COUNT(DISTINCT ...) over the proper join). | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., average distinct_dataset_count by author), join this view to an author-paper mapping that is one-row-per-(author,paper) (for example a normalized author-paper membership view that is guaranteed one row per author-paper). If the author mapping is many rows per (author,paper) (e.g., repeated name variants), first collapse it to unique (authorId, paperId) before joining, or aggregate after join using SUM(DISTINCT ...) / AVG by grouping appropriately. | If you need to join to another AGG view that is also one-row-per-paper (e.g., paper_coauthor_counts if it is one-row-per-paper), it is safe to join on paperId — both are at the same grain so measures remain aligned. If the sibling view is at a different grain, bring it to paper grain via aggregation before joining. | In planner terms: this view's grain = paperId (one row per paper). Only join without re-aggregation to other data sets that also have grain <= paperId where <= means 'one row per paper' (i.e., same or strictly one-row-per-paper). For any join target that is one-to-many relative to paper, either deduplicate the target to paper-level or re-aggregate the result to avoid duplicating distinct_dataset_count.

views.description: Per-paper counts of distinct datasets referenced by that paper (one row per paper).

views.name: paper_authorships_24
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.paperId AS paperId,
  w.authorId AS authorId,
  p.title AS title,
  p.year AS year,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  p.journalId AS journalId
FROM writes w
JOIN paper p ON p.paperId = w.paperId

params.description: A one-row-per (paperId, authorId) view listing a paper-author pair with the paper's title, year, venueId, and journalId.
params.when_to_use: List all authors of papers along with basic paper metadata (title, year, venueId, journalId). | Filter or aggregate at the paper-author grain (e.g., count authors per paper, list papers for an author). | Join paper-author pairs to author-level or paper-level dimensions without duplicating measures when those joins are 1:1 on the appropriate key. | Use as the input to further aggregation (e.g., produce per-paper metrics or per-author metrics) because the view is already at the atomic paper-author grain.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from writes.paperId (base table 'writes'). | authorId: identifier of the author (contributor) — derived from writes.authorId (base table 'writes'). | title: paper title — derived from paper.title (base table 'paper'). | year: publication year of the paper — derived from paper.year (base table 'paper'). | venueId: identifier of the venue (conference/meeting) associated with the paper — derived from paper.venueId (base table 'paper'). | journalId: identifier of the journal associated with the paper — derived from paper.journalId (base table 'paper').
params.grounded_columns: writes.paperId | writes.authorId | paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.year | paper.venueId | paper.journalId
params.metric: row-level: no aggregated numeric measures are defined in this view; all outputs are direct column projections from base tables. | If you derive counts/aggregates on top of this view, define them explicitly (e.g., num_authors_per_paper = COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) GROUP BY paperId) because this view contains one row per (paperId, authorId).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a paper-level dimension or view on paperId (for example paper_core, paper_core_5, paper_with_venue_journal) — safe because this view is one-row-per (paperId, authorId) and joining to a one-row-per-paper relation will not multiply rows beyond the inherent paper-author multiplicity. | cardinality-SAFE: join to an author-level dimension or view on authorId (for example author_identity) — safe because joining to a one-row-per-author relation preserves the one-row-per (paperId, authorId) grain and does not duplicate measures. | unsafe-without-aggregation: do NOT join this view directly to any relation that is one-to-many from (paperId, authorId) (for example a table of author_aliases where an author can have multiple aliases, or a detailed paper revision history where paperId appears many times) unless you first aggregate or deduplicate the many-side. Such joins would multiply rows and any derived counts will be inflated. | unsafe-without-aggregation: do NOT join to a relation that is many-to-many on either paperId or authorId without explicitly re-aggregating or deduplicating on the many side (for example joins to paper_authors_by_name or paper_author_names_agg must be used carefully: if they are many-per-(paperId,authorId) you must aggregate them before joining). | planner guidance: treat this view as the atomic (paperId, authorId) fact. To compute paper-level measures, GROUP BY paperId over this view. To compute author-level measures, GROUP BY authorId. When composing with sibling JOIN views, verify their grain — only join directly to views that are single-row-per-key on the join key to avoid accidental duplication.

views.description: A one-row-per (paperId, authorId) view listing a paper-author pair with the paper's title, year, venueId, and journalId.

views.name: paper_coauthor_counts_by_paper
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pam.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pam.authorId) AS distinct_author_count
FROM paper_author_membership AS pam
GROUP BY pam.paperId

params.description: Counts of distinct authors per paper (one row per paper).
params.when_to_use: Get the number of unique authors for a specific paper or set of papers. | Join as a measure when computing paper-level aggregates that need author counts (e.g., average coauthor count by venue) provided joins do not multiply rows. | Filter or rank papers by how many distinct authors they have. | Compose into downstream SQL that computes rates or ratios per paper (e.g., citations per author) while preserving per-paper granularity.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper (derived from paper_author_membership.paperId) | distinct_author_count: integer count of unique authors associated with the paper (derived from COUNT(DISTINCT paper_author_membership.authorId))
params.metric: distinct_author_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paper_author_membership.authorId) grouped by paper_author_membership.paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or 1:1 views keyed by paperId (for example paper_core or paper_core_5) on paperId — safe because paper_coauthor_counts_by_paper has exactly one row per paperId so joining these will not duplicate its measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to read-only selection/normalization views that are one-row-per-paper (e.g., paper_with_venue_journal, paper_core) on paperId — safe for the same reason. | do NOT join directly to paper_author_membership or any other paper-level one-to-many table/view (e.g., paper_authorships, paper_author_link) without re-aggregating, because those joins will duplicate paper_coauthor_counts_by_paper rows and inflate/duplicate the distinct_author_count measure. | do NOT join to sibling AGG views that are at a finer grain (multiple rows per paper) unless you first aggregate them to one row per paper or join through a deduplicated paper-level key, because joining to many-rows-per-paper sources will multiply this view's measures. | If you must combine with a one-to-many relationship on paperId, first aggregate the many-side to one row per paper (for example SUM, COUNT, MAX) and then join on paperId so aggregation semantics remain correct and distinct_author_count is not double-counted. | When composing further aggregations (e.g., computing average distinct_author_count by venue), use this view as the inner aggregation (one row per paper) and then GROUP BY the higher-level key (e.g., venue) — do not re-count authors at that stage; treat distinct_author_count as a derived metric to be aggregated with numeric aggregators (SUM, AVG) depending on the desired higher-level measure.

views.description: Counts of distinct authors per paper (one row per paper).

views.name: authors_by_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  author.authorId AS authorId,
  TRIM(author.authorName) AS authorName
FROM author

params.description: Provides one row per author with the author's identifier and cleaned (trimmed) name.
params.when_to_use: Get a list of authors (id + normalized name) for display or joining to author-level facts. | Use as the author dimension when composing author-level aggregates (e.g., paper counts per author) to attach author metadata. | Filter or look up authors by authorId or authorName before joining to author-level or paper-author tables.
params.output_schema: authorId: the unique identifier of the author, derived from base table column author.authorId | authorName: the author's name after trimming whitespace, derived from base table column author.authorName via TRIM(author.authorName)
params.metric: authorId = author.authorId | authorName = TRIM(author.authorName)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_papers_cohort (SEL) on authors_by_name.authorId = author_papers_cohort.authorId — safe because authors_by_name is one-row-per-author (grain = authorId) so joining to an author-level cohort preserves one row per author from this view, and any counts in the cohort view are pre-aggregated at authorId. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity (NORM) on authors_by_name.authorId = author_identity.authorId — safe because both are author-keyed, so this view's rows are not duplicated and author-level attributes align 1:1 or 1:0. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_author_membership (JOIN) or paper_authorships (JOIN) only when you intend to expand authors into their paper-level memberships; these joins are one-to-many (author -> papers) and WILL multiply authors_by_name rows. If you need author-level aggregated measures (e.g., number of papers), do not join directly — instead aggregate the paper-level table to authorId first (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY authorId) and then join the aggregated result back to authors_by_name to avoid duplication. | do NOT join authors_by_name directly to paper_core, paper_core_5, paper_with_venue_journal, paper_author_link, paper_authors_by_name, paper_author_names_agg, paper_coauthor_counts, or other paper-level tables without re-aggregation on the paper side because those are one-to-many relative to authorId and would multiply the author rows and any attached measures. | If composing further aggregates: to compute author-level metrics (e.g., total_papers), derive the metric from the paper-level source by aggregating by authorId (e.g., FROM paper_author_membership GROUP BY authorId COUNT(*) AS total_papers) and then join that aggregated result to authors_by_name ON authorId — this preserves correct cardinality and prevents double-counting. | When joining to sibling aggregate views (paper_coauthor_counts, paper_author_names_agg) ensure those sibling views are keyed at authorId; if they are aggregated at a different grain (e.g., paper), follow the same rule: aggregate to authorId before joining to authors_by_name.

views.description: Provides one row per author with the author's identifier and cleaned (trimmed) name.

views.name: paper_coauthors_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS coauthor_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS coauthor_ids,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS coauthor_names
FROM writes w
JOIN author a ON a.authorId = w.authorId
JOIN paper p ON p.paperId = w.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregation of its co-authors: count, list of coauthor ids, and list of coauthor names (one row per paperId).
params.when_to_use: Get the number of distinct co-authors for a given paperId or set of paperIds. | Retrieve the set/list of coauthor IDs or coauthor names for a paper. | Compose higher-level metrics per paper (e.g., join with paper metadata) without recounting co-authors. | Filter/segment papers by coauthor_count (e.g., papers with > N co-authors) and then join to other paper-level views.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the PK/grain of this view; identifies the paper this row describes. | coauthor_count: COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) — the number of distinct authors who wrote the paper (derived from writes.authorId aggregated per paper). | coauthor_ids: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) — a concatenated string of the distinct authorId values for the paper (derived from writes.authorId). | coauthor_names: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName) — a concatenated string of distinct author names for the paper (derived from author.authorName via joins).
params.metric: coauthor_count = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) GROUP BY paper.paperId | coauthor_ids = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) GROUP BY paper.paperId | coauthor_names = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName) GROUP BY paper.paperId
params.composition: Safe: join to paper_core (or any other paper-level view such as paper_core_5, paper_with_venue_journal) on paperId — safe because paper_coauthors_agg is one-row-per-paperId, so its measures (coauthor_count, lists) will not be duplicated. | Safe: join to other one-row-per-paper derived/normalized views (e.g., paper_author_membership when used as a paper-level summary) on paperId — only if the joined view is also guaranteed one-row-per-paper. | Unsafe: do NOT join directly to a writes (paper-author link) table or any other one-to-many detail (e.g., paper_authorships, paper_author_link) on paperId without re-aggregation — those joins would multiply rows per paper and therefore duplicate the coauthor_count and lists. If you must combine with one-to-many rows, re-aggregate after the join (e.g., SUM or MAX of measures after grouping by paperId) or join on paperId to a distinct/list of keys derived from writes to preserve cardinality. | Unsafe: do NOT join to tables that are one-to-many from paper (for example: detailed contribution records, per-author affiliations, or other author-level tables keyed to authorId) without first collapsing either side to paper-level aggregates. Joining author-level rows directly will multiply coauthor_count and invalidate distinct-based lists. | Guidance for planner composition: treat this view as a paper-level (grain=paperId) aggregate. When composing into larger queries, ensure any join keys preserve the one-to-one relationship per paperId (paper-level dimensions) or apply aggregation on the result of any one-to-many join to restore one row per paperId before consuming coauthor_count or list columns.

views.description: Per-paper aggregation of its co-authors: count, list of coauthor ids, and list of coauthor names (one row per paperId).

views.name: keyphrase_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  keyphrase.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId,
  keyphrase.keyphraseName AS keyphraseName
FROM keyphrase

params.description: Provides one row per keyphrase (id and name); answers questions about keyphrase identity and can be used as a base when joining keyphrase metadata to other tables or when aggregating measures by keyphrase.
params.when_to_use: Lookup the canonical keyphrase name given a keyphraseId | Filter or group other metrics by keyphraseId/keyphraseName | Compose into larger queries that need one-row-per-keyphrase dimensional information (e.g., counts of papers per keyphrase when joined to a paper-keyphrase association) | Serve as the dimension side in joins from fact/association tables keyed by keyphraseId
params.output_schema: keyphraseId: unique identifier for the keyphrase — derived from base column keyphrase.keyphraseId | keyphraseName: human-readable name/text of the keyphrase — derived from base column keyphrase.keyphraseName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or association tables that reference keyphraseId (for example, a hypothetical paper_keyphrase association table) on keyphraseId — safe because keyphrase_rows is one-row-per-keyphrase so joining it to many-row facts will not duplicate keyphrase_rows' rows (facts will multiply but keyphrase dimension remains one row per keyphrase). | You may join keyphrase_rows to other one-row-per-keyphrase normalized views (if any exist) on keyphraseId without causing duplication because both sides are keyed 1:1 on keyphraseId. | Do NOT join keyphrase_rows directly to any one-to-many child table (for example, a table that lists multiple associations per keyphrase) if you expect to preserve aggregated measures from keyphrase_rows — such a join will produce multiple rows per keyphrase and therefore multiply any metrics computed from keyphrase_rows unless you re-aggregate after the join. Instead, either: | - aggregate the child/association table up to keyphraseId first (so it becomes one-row-per-keyphrase) and then join, or | - join and then GROUP BY keyphraseId (and keyphraseName) to re-establish one-row-per-keyphrase before computing per-keyphrase metrics. | Examples of safe composition: join keyphrase_rows.keyphraseId = paper_keyphrase.keyphraseId then GROUP BY keyphrase_rows.keyphraseId to compute COUNT(paper_id) as papers_per_keyphrase. Unsafe without re-aggregation: joining keyphrase_rows to paper_keyphrase and selecting keyphrase_rows.keyphraseId plus an aggregate-less measure from keyphrase_rows — this will duplicate keyphrase rows across multiple associations.

views.description: Provides one row per keyphrase (id and name); answers questions about keyphrase identity and can be used as a base when joining keyphrase metadata to other tables or when aggregating measures by keyphrase.

views.name: paper_keyphrase_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paperKeyphrase.paperId AS paperId,
  paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId
FROM paperKeyphrase

params.description: Maps which keyphrases are associated with which papers (one row per paperId + keyphraseId).
params.when_to_use: Find all keyphrases for a given paper or set of papers. | Find all papers that contain a given keyphrase or set of keyphrases. | Compose with paper-level or keyphrase-level dimensions to add attributes (title, venue, author info) without changing the paper-keyphrase association. | Build aggregated metrics such as counts of keyphrases per paper or counts of papers per keyphrase by aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from paperKeyphrase.paperId | keyphraseId: identifier of the keyphrase — derived from paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId
params.metric: paperId = paperKeyphrase.paperId | keyphraseId = paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId | count_keyphrases_per_paper = COUNT(keyphraseId) GROUP BY paperId  -- derived by aggregating this view | count_papers_per_keyphrase = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY keyphraseId  -- derived by aggregating this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or paper_core_5, paper_with_venue_journal) on paperId — safe because paper_core is one-row-per-paper; joining will enrich each (paperId, keyphraseId) row with paper attributes without duplicating the paper-keyphrase associations. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity or paper_author_membership (after appropriate aggregation) on paperId — to attach author-level attributes aggregate author data to one-row-per-paper first (for example, authors_agg = AGG(authorId) GROUP BY paperId) so you do not multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_author_link or paper_authorships only if those views are known to be one-row-per-(paper,author). If they are one-row-per-(paper,author) they will multiply rows per author; re-aggregate after joining if you need to keep one row per (paperId, keyphraseId). | do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables/views (for example, paper_authors_by_name, paper_author_membership, paper_authorships, paper_coauthor_counts, paper_author_names_agg) without re-aggregation because those are one-to-many relative to paperId and will multiply the (paperId, keyphraseId) rows and therefore duplicate counts/measures. Instead: aggregate the many-side to one row per paper (or per keyphrase) before joining, or perform joins within a query that then re-aggregates back to the intended grain. | to count keyphrases per paper safely: SELECT paperId, COUNT(*) AS num_keyphrases FROM paper_keyphrase_link GROUP BY paperId — do not join additional many-side tables before this aggregation. | to count papers per keyphrase safely: SELECT keyphraseId, COUNT(*) AS num_papers FROM paper_keyphrase_link GROUP BY keyphraseId — same caution about joins applies.

views.description: Maps which keyphrases are associated with which papers (one row per paperId + keyphraseId).

views.name: keyphrase_paper_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  k.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pkp.paperId) AS paper_count
FROM keyphrase k
LEFT JOIN paperKeyphrase pkp ON pkp.keyphraseId = k.keyphraseId
GROUP BY k.keyphraseId

params.description: Provides the number of distinct papers associated with each keyphrase (one row per keyphraseId).
params.when_to_use: Get total distinct paper counts for a specific keyphrase or set of keyphraseIds. | Rank or filter keyphrases by how many papers mention them. | Compose higher-level reports that need a stable, one-row-per-keyphrase measure (e.g., join keyphrase metadata or compute rates per keyphrase). | Use as the aggregated base when joining keyphrase-level metrics into broader dashboards without recounting papers.
params.output_schema: keyphraseId: identifier for a keyphrase; sourced from keyphrase.keyphraseId (base table 'keyphrase'). | paper_count: count of distinct papers associated with that keyphrase; derived from COUNT(DISTINCT paperKeyphrase.paperId) where paperKeyphrase is joined to keyphrase on keyphraseId.
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperKeyphrase.paperId) grouped by keyphrase.keyphraseId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to keyphrase (or any one-row-per-keyphrase dimension) on keyphraseId — safe because this view is one-row-per-keyphraseId so its paper_count will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling aggregated views that are also one-row-per-keyphraseId (if present) on keyphraseId — safe because both sides are keyed at the same grain. | DO NOT join directly to paperKeyphrase (or any other one-to-many table keyed by paper or paperKeyphrase rows) without re-aggregating, because joining this AGG view to a table that has multiple rows per keyphraseId (for example paperKeyphrase, paper_authorships, or paper_author_membership) will multiply paper_count and produce incorrect totals. If you must join to a one-to-many table, re-aggregate after the join (for example, SUM(paper_count_contrib) or recompute COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) at the desired grain). | DO NOT join to paper-level tables (paper_core, paper_core_5, paper_with_venue_journal, etc.) on keyphraseId expecting paper_count to distribute across papers — those are many-to-one or many-to-many relative to keyphrase and would duplicate the measure. Instead, either: |   - join keyphrase metadata to this view (one-to-one) to enrich keyphrase rows, or |   - if you need per-paper metrics together with keyphrase counts, compute separate paper-level aggregations and then combine results at an appropriate grain with explicit aggregation (e.g., compute per-paper metrics, then aggregate to keyphraseId via COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) or an intersection table). | When composing with author-level or paper-author views (paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_author_link, paper_authors_by_name, paper_author_names_agg, author_papers_cohort, author_identity, author_papers_cohort_7): do not join directly on keyphraseId to those views unless those views are first reduced to one row per keyphraseId (e.g., by computing distinct counts or other aggregates per keyphraseId). Otherwise, the many-to-many relationships between keyphrases, papers, and authors will multiply paper_count. | If you need to combine this view with another aggregated view at a different grain (for example, a per-author aggregated view), perform a safe reduction step to a common grain (e.g., compute papers per (keyphraseId, authorId) in a separate aggregation) before joining; this prevents accidental duplication of counts.

views.description: Provides the number of distinct papers associated with each keyphrase (one row per keyphraseId).

views.name: paper_citation_impact_label
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.numCitedBy,
  CASE
    WHEN p.numCitedBy IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 1000 THEN 'very high'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 500 THEN 'high'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 100 THEN 'moderate'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 20 THEN 'low'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy >= 1 THEN 'very low'
    ELSE 'none'
  END AS impact_label
FROM paper_core p

params.description: Provides a per-paper citation count and a human-readable impact label based on that count.
params.when_to_use: Show the citation-based impact category for a given paper or list of papers. | Filter or group papers by citation impact buckets (e.g., 'high', 'moderate'). | Join with other paper-level dimensions (venue, title, authors) when you need a single row per paper that includes a citation-impact label. | Use as a reliable paper-level seed when composing further aggregations (e.g., counts of papers by impact_label) because the view is one-row-per-paper.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper identifier (derives from paper_core.paperId) | numCitedBy: raw citation count for the paper (derives from paper_core.numCitedBy) | impact_label: categorical label computed from numCitedBy with the mapping: NULL -> 'unknown', >=1000 -> 'very high', >=500 -> 'high', >=100 -> 'moderate', >=20 -> 'low', >=1 -> 'very low', else 'none' (derived expression in the view)
params.metric:
numCitedBy = paper_core.numCitedBy  -- direct pass-through of base column (no aggregation) | impact_label = CASE
    WHEN paper_core.numCitedBy IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN paper_core.numCitedBy >= 1000 THEN 'very high'
    WHEN paper_core.numCitedBy >= 500 THEN 'high'
    WHEN paper_core.numCitedBy >= 100 THEN 'moderate'
    WHEN paper_core.numCitedBy >= 20 THEN 'low'
    WHEN paper_core.numCitedBy >= 1 THEN 'very low'
    ELSE 'none'
  END  -- deterministic bucketization of numCitedBy
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any paper-level dimension or normalization (one-row-per-paper) on paperId — e.g., paper_core (already the source), paper_with_venue_journal, paper_core_5 — because those joins are 1:1 (or 1:0/1) with this view, so numCitedBy and derived impact_label will not be duplicated. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many child tables or views keyed by paperId (for example paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_author_link, paper_authors_by_name, paper_author_names_agg, paper_coauthor_counts) without first re-aggregating or otherwise handling multiplicity, because those joins will multiply rows per paper and thus duplicate paper-level measures. If you need aggregates by the child dimension (e.g., counts per author or author-affiliation), either: |   - aggregate the child table first to one row per paper (e.g., COUNT(*) AS contributor_count by paperId) and then join to this view on paperId, or |   - join and then re-aggregate at the paper level (e.g., GROUP BY paperId) to restore one row per paper before using numCitedBy as a measure. | Examples of safe composition patterns: |   - Safe: paper_citation_impact_label JOIN paper_with_venue_journal USING (paperId)  -- one-row-per-paper join preserves measures |   - Safe: (SELECT paperId, COUNT(*) AS author_count FROM paper_authorships GROUP BY paperId) JOIN paper_citation_impact_label USING (paperId)  -- child table pre-aggregated to one row per paper | Examples of unsafe direct joins (will duplicate measures unless re-aggregated): |   - UNSAFE: paper_citation_impact_label JOIN paper_authorships USING (paperId)  -- many authors per paper will multiply rows and duplicate numCitedBy/impact_label |   - UNSAFE: paper_citation_impact_label JOIN paper_author_membership USING (paperId)  -- membership is typically many-per-paper | Notes for planners: this view is semantically a SELECT (no aggregation) with a strict grain of one row per paperId. Treat numCitedBy and impact_label as paper-level attributes (not additive metrics); do not SUM them across joins without explicit intent (e.g., counting papers by impact_label should count rows, not sum numCitedBy).

views.description: Provides a per-paper citation count and a human-readable impact label based on that count.

views.name: paper_author_list_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(w.authorId) AS author_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(a.authorName, ', ') AS author_names
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregation of its authors: the number of authors and a concatenated list of author names for each paperId.
params.when_to_use: Get the count of authors for a specific paper or set of papers (e.g., how many authors wrote paper X). | Retrieve a human-readable, comma-delimited list of author names for display or reporting per paper. | Compose into higher-level queries that need one row per paper enriched with author_count and author_names (e.g., join to paper metadata or venue info). | Filter or rank papers by author_count (e.g., find papers with > N authors) without re-aggregating the writes/author tables.
params.output_schema: paperId: the unique identifier of the paper; derived from table paper.paperId (GROUP BY key). | author_count: integer count of distinct write relationships counted per paper; derived from COUNT(writes.authorId) as implemented in the view (COUNT(w.authorId)). | author_names: a single text string containing the paper's author names concatenated and separated by ', '; derived from GROUP_CONCAT(author.authorName, ', ').
params.metric: author_count = COUNT(writes.authorId) — SQL aggregate counting number of write rows per paper (NULL authorId values in writes will be ignored by COUNT). | author_names = GROUP_CONCAT(author.authorName, ', ') — string aggregation of authorName for rows joined to the paper, ordered by the database's default GROUP_CONCAT ordering (no explicit ORDER BY), producing a single delimited string per paper.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or any other view or table that is one-row-per paper) on paperId — safe because paper_author_list_agg is one-row-per-paperId, so joining on paperId will not duplicate author_count or author_names. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core_5 or paper_with_venue_journal on paperId — safe for the same reason (those are normalization/joined views that are expected to be one-row-per-paper). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling AGG views that are one-row-per-paper (for example paper_coauthor_counts if it is also one-row-per-paper) on paperId — safe provided the sibling view is one-row-per-paper. | unsafe-to-join-without-reaggregation: do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables or views keyed by paperId that expand rows (for example writes, paper_authorships, paper_author_membership, paper_author_link, paper_authors_by_name, or other JOINs that return multiple rows per paper) because those joins would multiply rows and therefore duplicate author_count and author_names. If you need data from such one-to-many sources, either: | - join the one-to-many source first and then re-aggregate (e.g., re-COMBINE with GROUP BY p.paperId), or | - aggregate the one-to-many source to one row per paperId before joining (e.g., an AGG sibling like paper_author_names_agg), | notes on duplicates: because author_count is computed from COUNT(writes.authorId) in the view, joining to any table that has multiple rows per paper without reducing it to one row per paper will falsely increase apparent counts when the combined rowset is then used directly (planner must preserve the view's one-row-per-paper grain). | ordering and determinism: author_names uses GROUP_CONCAT without an ORDER BY; if a deterministic name order is required before composing further analyses (for example to compare author lists), first produce an ordered aggregation at the source or use a sibling reshape/view that guarantees ordering (the planner should not assume any particular order when composing).

views.description: Per-paper aggregation of its authors: the number of authors and a concatenated list of author names for each paperId.
